title: Perimeter Anti-Theft and Panic Alarms: Overview
introduction: The perimeter alarm attracts attention with sound and flashing lamps, but those outputs do not finish together. I read it as a performance with a loud opening and a longer light show: a quiet horn alone does not mean the flashing phase has ended. This overview explains the triggers and output sequence, plus how panic activation differs. Arming, disarming and troubleshooting steps are outside its scope.

edits.text: The perimeter alarm deters unauthorized entry by sounding the horn and flashing all turn signals and interior courtesy lamps. With the alarm armed, unauthorized entry or motion detected inside the vehicle by the intrusion sensor activates the horn and lamps for 30 seconds. After 30 seconds, the horn stops, while the lamps continue flashing for up to 5 minutes.
edits.why: The armed condition matters when interpreting a trigger. The response then has distinct sound-and-light and light-only phases, so continued flashing after the horn stops fits the described sequence.

edits.text: The panic alarm operates similarly to the perimeter alarm, but it activates only when you use the panic button on the RKE (remote keyless entry) transmitter.
edits.why: I distinguish the alarms by what starts them. Panic activation comes from the transmitter's panic button; it does not, by itself, indicate unauthorized entry or detected interior motion.
